I am 65 years old, farming 10.1 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and talk to the dealer at the cooperative, but I still trust my own eyes more than any book. My family has nine people, and two of my sons work in a factory in Handan and send money home, but I do not count on that for buying inputs. I have 8 mu of flat land where I do wheat and maize double cropping, and 2.1 mu of sandy land near the well where I grow cotton. My wife and I do most of the work, but I hire two day-laborers for wheat harvest and maize planting because the window between crops is only a few days.

For the winter wheat, it is already in the ground. I ploughed that land last October and planted the improved Jimai variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang used last year — he got 580 kg per mu, better than my old seed. I put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and last week at jointing stage I topdressed with 20 kg urea per mu. I will irrigate three times total this season: the green-up water already happened in March, now I need one at booting and one at grain filling before harvest in early June. I spray twice — herbicide once, and one insecticide-fungicide mix if I see aphids or rust. I expect 550 kg per mu. I would rather spend the extra 30 yuan on urea than risk losing a hundred kilograms of grain.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in early June — there is no time to waste, so I rotary till the stubble instead of deep ploughing. I use one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu drilled with the seed, then at big trumpet stage I spread 23 kg urea per mu. That is what the dealer said everyone is doing, and it gave me 580 kg last year, so I am doing the same. Maize needs three irrigations: one right after planting if it does not rain, one at tasseling in late July, and one at grain filling in August. I spray twice: herbicide right after planting, and insecticide once when the borers come in July. I expect 600 kg per mu. Hybrid seed costs more, but the yield difference pays for itself.

For cotton on the 2.1 mu, I plant improved Bt cotton seed in late April. I rotary till that plot in spring because cotton roots need loose soil. I put down 50 kg compound fertilizer per mu and an extra 15 kg of potassium fertilizer per mu — the dealer told me cotton needs more potassium or the bolls drop. I topdress twice with 10 kg urea each time, once at flowering and once at boll setting. Cotton drinks a lot of water through the hot months, so I irrigate four times. I spray four times: even Bt cotton gets spider mites and wilt in this weather. I expect 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year I got 260 kg, so I am pushing it a little harder this year.

Everything costs money. A 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer is 150 yuan, urea is 120 yuan. Pumping water from the well costs electricity too. I keep a notebook and calculate every purchase. But I learned my lesson in 2013 when I tried to save 200 yuan on fertilizer — the wheat turned yellow and I lost 1,500 yuan in yield. Now I follow what works. If Lao Zhang adds more, I add more. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.
